Position Title: Research Fellow / Research Assistant

Research Centre: Brunel Interdisciplinary Power Systems (BIPS)

Department/College: Department of Engineering

Location: Brunel University of London, Uxbridge Campus

Salary:  Grade R1 

Research Assistant: £37,810 to £40,956 per annum inclusive of London Weighting

Research Fellow: £42,068 to £49,478 per annum inclusive of London Weighting with potential to progress to £53,766 per annum, inclusive of London Weighting, through sustained exceptional contribution.

Hours: Full-time

Planned start date: 1 February 2027       

Contract Type: Fixed term for 12 months

Brunel University of London was established in 1966 and is a leading multidisciplinary research-intensive technology university delivering economic, social and cultural benefits.

For more information please visit: https://www.brunel.ac.uk/about/our-history/home

The new appointment will be associated with the internationally recognised Brunel Interdisciplinary Power Systems (BIPS) Research Centre within the Department of Engineering. The College of Engineering, Design and Physical Sciences (CEDPS) is one of the largest and most successful in the UK, with close to 5,000 undergraduate and postgraduate students. Department of Engineering is a vibrant and successful Department within CEDPS.

We are looking to recruit a Research Fellow / Research Assistant to work on the project “Climate Resilient Heat Electrification for Net-Zero Emission Whole Energy Systems (RENEW)”, funded by UKRI and carried out in collaboration with Newcastle University and Imperial College London. The project is coordinated by Dr Marko Aunedi on behalf of Brunel University of London in the UK.

Applicants are expected to hold a PhD in an appropriate area and have expertise in one or more of the following areas: energy system modelling and optimisation, power system analysis, renewable energy, transmission and distribution system operation, energy storage, low-carbon energy technologies or other closely related areas. You will be a self-motivated, but highly collaborative researcher. Strong communication and interpersonal skills, fluency in English and an ability to work independently are essential. Candidates will be expected to demonstrate a good track record in project management, presenting their work, report writing and research publications. Outstanding candidates without a PhD but having directly relevant research or practical experience are also welcome to apply.

We offer a generous annual leave package plus discretionary University closure days, excellent training and development opportunities as well as a great occupational pension scheme and a range of health-related support. The University is committed to a hybrid working approach.

Closing date for applications: 30 November 2026

Interviews are expected to take place during the week commencing 7 December 2026 in person.

For further details about the post including the Job Description and Person Specification and to apply please visit https://careers.brunel.ac.uk

If you have any technical issues please contact us at: hrsystems@brunel.ac.uk

Brunel University London is fully committed to creating and sustaining a fully inclusive workforce culture. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds and communities, we particularly welcome applicants who are currently under- represented in our workforce.

Job Description - Postdoctoral Research Associate in onboard carbon capture and storage (26001352)
Job Description
 
Postdoctoral Research Associate in onboard carbon capture and storage (Job Number: 26001352)
Department of Engineering
Grade 7: - £39,560 to £46,970 per annum
Fixed Term - Full Time
Contract Duration: until 31 March 2028
Contracted Hours per Week: 35
Closing Date: 16-Nov-2026, 11:59:00 PM
Disclosure and Barring Service Requirement: Not Applicable.
 

Working at Durham University  

A globally outstanding centre of teaching and research excellence, a warm and friendly place to work, a unique and historic setting – Durham is a university like no other.

As one of the UK’s leading universities, Durham is an incredible place to define your career. The University is located within a beautiful historic city, home to a UNESCO World Heritage Site, and surrounded by stunning countryside. Our talented scholars and researchers from around the world are tackling global issues and making a difference to people's lives.  

We believe that inspiring our people to do outstanding things at Durham enables Durham people to do outstanding things in the world. Being a part of Durham is about more than just the success of the University, it’s also about contributing to the success of the city, county and community.

Our University Strategy is built on three pillars of research, education and wider student experience, but also on our keen sense of community and of inspiring others to achieve their potential. 

Our Purpose and Values

We want our University to be a place where people can be free to be themselves, no matter what their identity or background. Together, we celebrate difference, value one another and are each responsible for creating an inclusive community that is respectful and fair for all.

Find out more about the benefits of working at the University and what it is like to live and work in the Durham area on our Why Join Us? - Information Page

The Role and Department

The Department of Engineering is highly ranked in the UK with an outstanding reputation for excellence in teaching, research and employability of our students. Ranked 21st in REF2021 in terms of grade point average, the Engineering Department has been ranked in 6th position by the Guardian University Guide 2026, 7th by the Times and Sunday Times Good University Guide 2026 and 24th globally in the QS World University Rankings: Sustainability 2026.

Professor Tony Roskilly leads a large Energy Systems Group within the Department of Engineering, comprising academic, post-doctoral research, administrative and technical staff. The Group’s collaborative research activities are also supported by researchers from Anthropology, Chemistry, Earth Sciences, Biological Sciences and Durham University Business School. It has a successful track record of attracting funding, primarily from the Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council (EPSRC), Innovate UK, the EU and industry.

For more information, please visit our Department pages at Department of Engineering - Durham University.

The Role

The Department seeks to appoint a Grade 7 Post-Doctoral Research Associate in onboard carbon capture and storage to contribute to this active research environment. We welcome applications from candidates with experience and expertise in onboard carbon capture and storage, life cycle assessment, carbon accounting, and circular economy. This post offers an exciting opportunity to make an important contribution to the development of the Department’s research, while providing excellent opportunities to develop your career within an ambitious and progressive institution.

The position is funded within the UK Clean Maritime Research Hub with financial support from the Department for Transport and EPSRC) to support policy-driven research on life cycle greenhouse gas intensity of marine fuels. The successful candidate will be line-managed by Professor Tony Roskilly. The candidate and will work closely with the project team to deliver high-quality research outputs. The candidate will be responsible for completing assigned project tasks on time, within budget and in line with the project objectives.

Key responsibilities:

To understand and convey material of a specialist or highly technical nature relating to onboard carbon capture and storage, life cycle assessment, carbon accounting, and circular economy to the team or group of people through presentations and discussions that leads to the presentation of research papers in conferences and publications.
To prepare and deliver presentations on research activities, methods and findings to audiences which may include research sponsors, academic and non-academic audiences.
To publish high quality outputs, including papers for submission to peer reviewed journals and papers for presentation at conferences and workshops under the direction of the Principal Investigator or Grant-holder.
To assist with the development of research objectives and proposals.
To conduct individual and collaborative research projects under the direction of the Principal Investigator or Grant-holder, including developing accounting frameworks that track carbon sources and sinks; defining accounting rules and developing modelling tool development; performing simulation and undertaking case studies.
To work with the Principal Investigator or Grant-holder and other colleagues in the research group, as appropriate, to identify knowledge and data gaps, develop robust and transparent accounting frameworks and methodologies, and advance the research portfolio in onboard carbon capture and storage.
To deal with problems that may affect the achievement of research objectives and deadlines by discussing with the Principal Investigator or Grant-holder and offering creative or innovative solutions.
To liaise with research colleagues and make internal and external contacts to develop knowledge and understanding to obtain technical evidence, improve understanding and form relationships for future research collaboration.
To plan and manage own research activity, research resources in collaboration with others and contribute to the planning of research projects, and maintain clear records of data sources, assumptions, methods, models, and research outputs.
To deliver training in research techniques/approaches to peers, visitors and students as appropriate.
To be involved in student supervision, as appropriate, and assist with the assessment of the knowledge of students.
To contribute to fostering a collegial and respectful working environment which is inclusive and welcoming and where everyone is treated fairly with dignity and respect.
To engage in wider citizenship to support the department and wider discipline.
To engage in continuing professional development by participation in the undergraduate or postgraduate teaching programmes or by membership of departmental committees, etc. and by attending relevant training and development courses.

·        Any other reasonable duties.

This post is fixed term, which will commence as soon as possible and terminate on the 31/03/2028. 

The post-holder is employed to work on research/a research project which will be led by another colleague. Whilst this means that the post-holder will not be carrying out independent research in his/her own right, the expectation is that they will contribute to the advancement of the project, through the development of their own research ideas/adaptation and development of research protocols.

Working at Durham 

A competitive salary is only one part of the many fantastic benefits you will receive if you join the University.

You’ll receive 30 days annual leave per year in addition to 8 public holidays and 4 customary days per year – a total of 42 days per year. The University closes between Christmas and New Year.

We offer a generous pension scheme, and as a new member of staff you will be automatically enrolled into the University Superannuation Scheme (USS).

No matter how you travel to work, we have you covered.  We have ample parking across campus, a cycle to work scheme which helps you to buy a bike and discount with local bus and train companies. You can also take advantage of our cost-effective and environmentally friendly Tusker Car Benefit Scheme, allowing you to lease a brand-new electric or hybrid vehicle with savings on tax and National Insurance.

We have a genuine commitment to developing our colleagues professionally and personally.  There is a comprehensive range of development courses, apprenticeships and access to qualifications and routes to develop your career in the University.  All staff have dedicated annual time to concentrate on their personal development opportunities.

We provide wide-ranging health and wellbeing support including discounted membership for our state-of-the-art sport and gym facilities and access to a 24-7 Employee Assistance Programme.

Our on-site nursery is rated Outstanding by Ofsted, and you can access holiday camps for children aged 5-16.

Our family-friendly policies, including maternity and adoption leave, are among the most generous in the higher education sector (and likely above and beyond many employers).

We offer all staff the opportunity to take part in volunteering activities to make a difference in the local community.

You can access exclusive discounts via our benefits portal including money off at supermarkets, high street retailers, IT products such as Apple, eating out and days out at various attractions.

Various salary sacrifice schemes are also available to help you take advantage of tax savings on benefits.

If you are moving to Durham, you may be eligible for help with removal costs, and we have a dedicated team who can help you with the practicalities such as house hunting and schools.  If you need a visa, we cover most visa costs and offer an interest-free loan scheme to pay for dependant visas.

Discover more about our total rewards and benefits package here.

Durham University is committed to equality, diversity and inclusion

Equality, diversity, and inclusion (EDI) are a key component of the University’s Strategy and a central part of everything we do.  We also live by our Purpose and Values and our Staff Code of Conduct.  At Durham we actively work towards providing an environment where our staff and students can study, work and live in a community which is supportive and inclusive.

We welcome and encourage applications from those who are currently under-represented in our work force, including people with disabilities and from racially minoritised ethnic groups.

If you have taken a career break or periods of leave that may have impacted on the volume and recency of your research outputs and other activities, such as maternity, adoption or parental leave, you may wish to disclose this in your application. The selection committee will take this into account when evaluating your application.

The University has been awarded the Disability Confident Leader status. If you are a candidate with a disability, we are committed to ensuring fair treatment throughout the recruitment process. We will make adjustments to support the interview process wherever it is reasonable to do so and, where successful, reasonable adjustments will be made to support people within their role. 

Contact Information:

Professor Tony Roskilly

Anthony.p.roskilly@durham.ac.uk

Contact information for technical difficulties when submitting your application 

If you encounter technical difficulties when using the online application form, we prefer you send enquiries by email.  Please send your name along with a brief description of the problem you’re experiencing to e.recruitment@durham.ac.uk 

Alternatively, you may call 0191 334 6801 from the UK, or +44 191 334 6801 from outside the UK. This number operates during the hours of 09.00 and 17.00 Monday to Friday, UK time.  We will normally respond within one working day (Monday to Friday, excluding UK public holidays).  

How to Apply  

To progress to the assessment stage, candidates must evidence each of the essential criteria required for the role in the person specification below. It will be at the discretion of the recruiting panel as to whether they will also consider any desirable criteria, but we would urge candidates to provide evidence for all criteria.  

While some criteria will be considered at the shortlisting stage, other criteria may be considered later in the assessment process, such as questions at interview.  

Submitting your application 

We prefer to receive applications online.   We will update you about your application at various points throughout the selection process, via automated emails from our e-recruitment system. Please check your spam/junk folder periodically to make sure you have not missed any of our updates.

What to Submit 

All applicants are asked to submit: 

a CV and cover letter which details your experience, skills, and achievements in meeting (or the potential to meet) the criteria set out below.

 

Next Steps 

Short-listed candidates will be invited to the University, either virtually or in-person and will have the opportunity to meet key members of the Department.  The assessment for the post will normally include a presentation to the panel followed by an interview and we anticipate that the assessments and interviews will take place over two days. 

In the event that you are unable to attend in person on the date offered, it may not be possible to offer you an interview on an alternative date. 

Please note that in submitting your application Durham University will be processing your data. We would ask you to consider the relevant University Privacy Statement Job Applicants/Potential Job Applicants - Durham University which provides information on the collation, storing and use of data.   

Durham University is a UKVI sponsor. Applicants who require sponsorship to work in the UK should note that not all roles are eligible. Further information on visa requirements and eligibility can be found on the UKVI website.

Person Specification

Essential Criteria:

Qualifications

A PhD (or be close to submission) in Marine, Mechanical, Chemical, Systems or Environmental Engineering, or a related subject.

Experience

Experience in compiling, analysing and interpretating complex datasets, and conducting attributional and consequential life cycle assessment of marine energy systems.
Experience in carbon accounting and the traceability of fossil, biogenic and atmospheric carbon sources and sinks, assessing carbon capture, interim storage, offloading, transport, permanent storage and captured CO₂ utilisation pathways through synthetic and recycled-carbon fuels using life cycle approaches
Demonstrable ability to work independently and collaboratively within multidisciplinary research teams to deliver research objectives and outputs.
Demonstrable ability to write material of a quality commensurate with publication in highly-ranked journals.
Demonstrable ability to present research papers at conferences and communicate complex information to specialists and within the wider academic community.

Skills

Demonstrable ability to develop transparent and robust methodologies, models using professional software, and analytical frameworks to inform decision making.
Ability to work independently on own initiative and to strict deadlines.
Excellent interpersonal and communication skills.

Desirable Criteria 

Experience

Experience in integrating circular economy concepts with life cycle assessment and implementing appropriate allocation approaches within relevant studies.
Strong publication record in peer-reviewed journals, commensurate with stage of career.
Experience of overseeing students with respect to the development of their practical/research skills e.g. acting as a demonstrator; supervising student projects/practicals.

Skills

Demonstrable ability to plan and manage independent research. 
Demonstrable ability to develop research proposals and designs in collaboration with other academics.

Postdoctoral Research Associate in Medicinal Chemistry

Job id: 161585. Salary: £45,031 - £47,379 per annum inclusive of London weighting allowance.

Posted: 26 October 2026. Closing date: 08 November 2026.

Business unit: Faculty of Life Sciences & Medicine. Department: Institute of Pharmaceutical Science.

Contact details: Professor Miraz Rahman. k.miraz.rahman@kcl.ac.uk

Location: Waterloo Campus. Category: Research.

Back to job search

About us

King’s College London is a world-leading Russell Group university with an outstanding international reputation for research and education. This post will be based in the Drug Discovery Department within the Institute of Pharmaceutical Science and will form part of a multidisciplinary collaboration between Professor Miraz Rahman and Professor Julian Naglik in the Centre for Host-Microbiome Interactions. The project brings together complementary expertise in medicinal chemistry, drug discovery, fungal pathogenesis and host–pathogen interactions, providing an excellent environment for collaborative and translational research. 

About The Role

Candida albicans is a major fungal pathogen that can cause severe morbidity and life-threatening infection. A key virulence factor is candidalysin, a peptide toxin secreted by C. albicans hyphae that drives epithelial damage, cell activation and mucosal inflammation. 

The postdoctoral researcher will play a central role in the discovery and optimisation of peptide and peptidomimetic inhibitors that neutralise candidalysin activity. The role will focus on the design, synthesis, purification and characterisation of inhibitor series, working within an iterative medicinal chemistry programme informed by computational modelling, biophysical measurements and biological activity.

The researcher will develop and optimise synthetic routes, undertake parallel synthesis where appropriate, and scale up selected compounds for detailed biophysical and biological evaluation. They will use analytical and preparative HPLC, LC-MS, NMR and other appropriate techniques to confirm compound identity, purity and quality. A major part of the role will be to interpret emerging structure–activity relationships and use experimental data to guide subsequent inhibitor design.

The researcher will work closely with the computational chemist and with Professor Julian Naglik’s team, who will evaluate inhibitor activity in relevant biological models. This close integration of chemistry, modelling, biophysics and infection biology will support rapid prioritisation and optimisation of compounds with the greatest therapeutic potential.

The post is particularly suited to a synthetic organic or medicinal chemist with strong practical experience in compound synthesis and characterisation. Previous experience in peptide or peptidomimetic chemistry would be advantageous but is not essential.

The researcher will be funded by the BBSRC and based in the laboratory of Professor Miraz Rahman at King’s College London, where they will undertake independent, original research within a multidisciplinary drug-discovery programme. 

This is a full time post (35 Hours per week), and you will be offered an a fixed term contract until 31st December 2028.

About You

To be successful in this role, we are looking for candidates to have the following skills and experience: 

Essential Criteria: 

PhD in Medicinal Chemistry, Pharmaceutical Sciences, Organic Chemistry or a closely related discipline (candidates who have recently submitted their PhD thesis are eligible to apply).
 Research experience in synthetic medicinal chemistry, with demonstrated expertise in the design and synthesis of bioactive molecules.
Knowledge and practical experience of compound characterisation using NMR, mass spectrometry, HPLC and other appropriate analytical techniques.
Experience in analytical and preparative HPLC/LC-MS methods for purification, characterisation and quality assessment of synthetic compounds.
Track record of high-quality research, including publications in peer-reviewed journals of international standing.
Experience in medicinal chemistry optimisation, including generation and interpretation of structure–activity relationships and iterative design–make–test cycles.
Excellent organisational, communication and teamwork skills, with the ability to work effectively within a multidisciplinary research team.

Desirable Criteria: 

Experience in chemistry laboratory management, including electronic inventory maintenance.
Record of presenting scientific research at national and/or international conferences.
Experience in operating and maintaining LC-MS systems.
Excellent interpersonal skills.
Record of supervising, appraising, coaching and mentoring research students.

Downloading a copy of our Job Description

Full details of the role and the skills, knowledge and experience required can be found in the Job Description document, provided at the bottom of the page. This document will provide information of what criteria will be assessed at each stage of the recruitment process.

* Please note that this is a PhD level role but candidates who have submitted their thesis and are awaiting award of their PhDs will be considered. In these circumstances the appointment will be made at Grade 5, spine point 30 with the title of Research Assistant. Upon confirmation of the award of the PhD, the job title will become Research Associate and the salary will increase to Grade 6.

Further Information

The Equality Act of 2010 protects the rights of our students and staff and provides a framework to fulfil our duties to eliminate unlawful discrimination, harassment and victimisation and in addition, to advance equality of opportunity and foster good relations between those who share a protected characteristic and those who do not. When engaging in the robust exchange of ideas, we ask that our community is mindful of our Dignity at King’s guidance.

We ask all candidates to submit a copy of their CV, and a supporting statement, detailing how they meet the essential criteria listed in the person specification section of the job description. If we receive a strong field of candidates, we may use the desirable criteria to choose our final shortlist, so please include your evidence against these where possible.

Applicants may use AI tools to support preparation of their application, for example to research the role or structure written responses. However, applications must reflect the applicant’s own work and experience. AI tools should not be used during interviews or assessment activities unless this has been agreed in advance as a reasonable adjustment. Further guidance on the use of AI in recruitment can be found here.

The role

About Us

King’s College London is a world-leading Russell Group university with an outstanding international reputation for research and education. This post will be based in the Drug Discovery Department within the Institute of Pharmaceutical Science and will form part of a multidisciplinary collaboration between Professor Miraz Rahman and Professor Julian Naglik in the Centre for Host-Microbiome Interactions. The project brings together complementary expertise in medicinal chemistry, drug discovery, fungal pathogenesis and host–pathogen interactions, providing an excellent environment for collaborative and translational research. 

About The Role

Candida albicans is a major fungal pathogen that can cause severe morbidity and life-threatening infection. A key virulence factor is candidalysin, a peptide toxin secreted by C. albicans hyphae that drives epithelial damage, cell activation and mucosal inflammation. 

The postdoctoral researcher will lead the computational chemistry component of a multidisciplinary programme to identify and optimise peptide, peptidomimetic and small-molecule inhibitors of candidalysin. The role will combine molecular modelling, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulations and structure-based design to understand candidalysin structure, conformational behaviour and interactions with candidate inhibitors.

The researcher will design and optimise peptide and peptidomimetic inhibitors, identify key residues and structural features governing binding and activity, and undertake virtual screening of small-molecule libraries to identify new chemical matter with potential to inhibit candidalysin function. Where appropriate, they will investigate candidalysin in membrane-associated environments and examine how inhibitors may alter toxin conformation, oligomerisation, membrane interaction or other processes required for activity.

A major focus of the role will be the integration of computational predictions with biophysical and biological data. The researcher will rationalise structure–activity relationships, explain differences in inhibitor potency and activity, and use emerging experimental results to refine computational models and guide subsequent design cycles. They will also apply appropriate computational methods to assess binding interactions, conformational behaviour, physicochemical properties and compound developability.

The researcher will work closely with the synthetic medicinal chemist and with Professor Julian Naglik’s team to prioritise compounds for synthesis and biological evaluation, helping to drive an efficient design–make–test cycle.

The researcher will be funded by the BBSRC and based in the laboratory of Professor Miraz Rahman at King’s College London, where they will undertake independent, original research within a multidisciplinary drug-discovery programme. 

This is a full time post (35 Hours per week), and you will be offered a fixed term contract until 31/12/2027.

PhD in Computational Chemistry, Medicinal Chemistry, Chemical Biology or a closely related discipline (candidates who have recently submitted their PhD thesis are eligible to apply).

Experience in the computational design and evaluation of peptides, peptidomimetics and/or small-molecule inhibitors, including interpretation of structure–activity relationships.
Proficiency with relevant computational chemistry software packages, such as Schrödinger Suite, AutoDock Vina, BIOVIA Discovery Studio or equivalent platforms.
Ability to integrate computational predictions with biophysical, biochemical and biological data to rationalise inhibitor activity and guide iterative compound design.
Track record of high-quality research, including publications in peer-reviewed journals of international standing.
Excellent organisational, analytical, communication and teamwork skills, with the ability to work effectively within a multidisciplinary research team.

Desirable Criteria: 

Experience in advanced molecular dynamics approaches, membrane-associated simulations, binding-energy calculations and/or other computational methods relevant to peptide–protein interactions.
Record of presenting scientific research at national and/or international conferences.
Experience in computational workflow development, scripting, cheminformatics and/or bioinformatics approaches relevant to drug discovery.
Experience of multidisciplinary collaboration with synthetic chemists, biophysicists and/or biological scientists, particularly in structure-guided inhibitor discovery.
Experience of supervising, mentoring or supporting MSc, PhD or other research students.

About Us

The Faculty of Life Sciences & Medicine at King’s College London seeks to appoint a Research Fellow in the Comprehensive Cancer Centre, which is the academic arm of one of the leading cancer centres in Europe bringing together world-class clinical services delivered by our NHS partners, with research and education for the benefit of cancer patients in South East London and beyond. 

​ 

The Wellcome project to accelerate cutting-edge bioimaging technology development, is a five-year cross-disciplinary programme, led by Professor Maddy Parsons from the School of Basic & Medical Biosciences. It will develop pioneering approaches to enable the creation of full molecular ‘maps’ of disease tissue, spanning multiple scales from whole organ down to individual molecules.

The programme will combine MRI-based clinical imaging of patients with emerging spatial methods that capture the underlying cellular and molecular activity within tissues in intricate detail. By combining data from these diverse imaging approaches using advanced computational and AI-driven tools, the team aim to reveal how cells interact with their environment and how these interactions drive disease.

About The Role

We are seeking a computational scientist with a strong machine learning background to develop new methods for spatial transcriptomics (ST). Working within the Wellcome-funded bioimaging programme, you will design, implement and validate AI and mathematical approaches that turn high-dimensional spatially resolved molecular data from platforms such as 10x Xenium into quantitative descriptions of tissue organisation and disease.

The role focuses on building models and frameworks that treat tissue as a spatial and geometric object. We are particularly interested in bringing ideas from geometric and unsupervised deep learning, spatial statistics and topology to bear on how cells organise into neighbourhoods, how they interact, and how these local patterns give rise to tissue architecture. You will also lead work on integrating ST with digital pathology and clinical imaging, linking molecular, cellular and organ-level scales.

You will join a multidisciplinary team at King's and partner institutions, where computational scientists and mathematicians work alongside pathologists, clinicians and experimental biologists. A central part of the role is turning biological and clinical questions into well-posed computational problems, and making sure the resulting methods are robust, reproducible and able to scale on high-performance computing. We expect you to build an independent research profile, publishing your methods in leading venues and sharing them as open-source software, while helping to shape new grant applications and supervising PhD students and junior researchers.

This is a full time and you will be offered an a fixed term contract until 31 March 2031.

About You

To be successful in this role, we are looking for candidates to have the following skills and experience:

Essential criteria

A PhD in a quantitative discipline (e.g. computer science, mathematics, statistics, physics or engineering), or in computational biology with a strong methodological component.
A track record of developing novel AI/machine-learning or mathematical/statistical methods, shown by publications in peer-reviewed journals or leading machine-learning conferences.
Significant experience modelling spatially defined data, ideally imaging-based spatial transcriptomics (e.g. Xenium).
Strong expertise in modern machine learning (e.g. graph neural networks, representation/self-supervised learning, generative models), with proficiency in Python and a deep-learning framework such as PyTorch.
Experience developing reproducible, scalable and open-source research software, including on high-performance and GPU computing.
A proven ability to lead research projects, collaborate with academic partners and supervise researchers.

Desirable criteria

Expertise in topological and geometric approaches to tissue architecture, such as persistent homology, discrete curvature and Ricci flow, graph Laplacians and spectral methods, or optimal transport.
Experience in spatial statistics (e.g. point processes, spatial autocorrelation, Gaussian processes) or probabilistic modelling of spatial data.
Experience integrating multimodal or multiscale data, e.g. spatial transcriptomics with H&E/digital pathology, multiplexed imaging or MRI, including use of pathology or single-cell foundation models.
Experience with image-level processing of spatial data, such as cell segmentation and denoising.
Experience presenting complex quantitative methods to multidisciplinary audiences and mentoring researchers from non-computational backgrounds.

We are seeking an enthusiastic and motivated researcher to join the laboratory of Dr Suzannah Rihn at the Cambridge Institute of Therapeutic Immunology and Infectious Disease (CITIID), University of Cambridge.

Emerging and re-emerging viruses pose a continuing threat to human health. Understanding the molecular mechanisms that enable viruses to cross species barriers, adapt to new hosts and establish infections in humans is essential for improving our preparedness for future epidemics and pandemics. Our research uses a combination of molecular virology, cell biology and experimental models of virus infection to investigate the interactions between viruses and their hosts that determine the potential for viral emergence.

The successful candidate will contribute to an exciting research programme investigating the molecular determinants of viral cross-species transmission. Working as part of a collaborative research team, they will use a range of experimental approaches to investigate how viral and host factors influence infection, replication and adaptation. The project will provide opportunities to develop expertise in molecular virology, including cell culture, molecular cloning, viral reverse genetics and functional assays of virus infection.

The postholder will be expected to plan and conduct experiments, analyse and interpret data, maintain accurate research records and contribute to the preparation of scientific manuscripts and presentations. They will also participate in laboratory meetings, contribute to the wider scientific activities of the group and collaborate with colleagues within CITIID and beyond.

Applicants should have, or be close to obtaining, a PhD in biological, biochemical or biomedical sciences, with relevant experience in molecular biology or virology. We are particularly interested in candidates with experience studying virus infection, a strong background in experimental molecular virology and an emerging track record of scientific publications or presentations. Role Description

Help us bring four strands of AI research together into one working flight-deck assistant, and test it with airline pilots in our research flight simulator.

TRUST-IA is a research project funded by the European Union’s Horizon Europe programme and coordinated by Cranfield, with university partners in Germany and France, and Rolls-Royce. It is developing an intelligent assistant to help airline pilots manage the engines, both in normal flight and when an engine fails. The assistant has four parts, each developed by a different partner: software that decides how the assistant should behave; monitoring of aircraft and engine condition; monitoring of the pilots; workload and trust from physiological and behavioural measures; and interaction through voice, gesture and mixed reality.

You will bring these parts together in Cranfield’s Future Systems Simulator. You will build the software platform and automated tests that let them run as one system in real time, set up the flight scenarios, and run simulator trials with pilots to show that the integrated assistant works and is safe to use. You will have a PhD in aerospace engineering or a related engineering subject, or equivalent research experience, and a background in aircraft modelling and simulation, flight dynamics or flight control. You will be a capable programmer (for example in C#, C++ or Python), and experience with Unity would be a real advantage. Research Associate – The Emotional Life of Clothes - (9677)

About the Institute

Manchester Fashion Institute, part of Manchester Metropolitan University, is a leading global fashion school spanning design, communication, business, technology and heritage, with recent investment in digital facilities, new academic appointments and a multimillion-pound fashion robotics lab. We value diversity and welcome applications from all backgrounds, particularly from groups underrepresented in higher education.

Our research community is thriving, with fashion contributing to an Art & Design REF submission ranked second in the UK for research power; across the University, 90% of our research is rated world-leading or internationally excellent. The successful candidate will become a visiting scholar within the F/fashion Narratives Research Group, with access to research training and career development opportunities at both Manchester Met. and the University of Manchester.  

About the Project

Dr Benjamin Wild (Project Lead), with Professor Emma Banister (University of Manchester), Dr Jo Jenkinson and Jolene Sheehan (Joy Ethic) as Project Co-Leads, has secured ESRC funding for ‘The Emotional Life of Clothes', a 30-month project exploring how people's emotional connections with clothing can support circular fashion and sustainable lifestyles. Reframing people as ‘wearers' rather than ‘consumers', the project will build new knowledge to inform narrative and policy strategies for how we buy, repair, recycle and replace clothes. Focused on Greater Manchester, the UK's ‘fast-fashion capital', it brings together Manchester Met, the University of Manchester, community groups, fashion intermediaries, Greater Manchester Combined Authority (GMCA) and Heard Storytelling, with outputs feeding into GMCA policy and a national industry report. 

 Further project details: https://fashionnarratives.mmu.ac.uk/the-emotional-life-of-clothes-leveraging-the-connection-between-emotion-and-clothing-to-support-circular-fashion-through-sustainable-lifestyles/

About the Role

This is a rare opportunity to join the project as its sole full-time researcher, working across the entire research cycle from typology-building and community fieldwork through to co-authored publications and public dissemination. Managed by the Project Lead, you will play an integral role in theoretical framing, participant recruitment, data collection and management, and project outputs. The role is full time (35 hours per week) and fixed term for 29 months, with an anticipated start date on or before 31 December 2026.

The role is based at Manchester Met, with hybrid/home working available on days without in-person commitments (e.g. fieldwork, training, meetings and engagement activities). Evening and weekend work is likely to be required, along with regular travel across Greater Manchester and occasional travel further afield for advisory board meetings and conferences. 

Key Responsibilities

Help build a typology of narratives about emotion and clothing consumption, contributing to the project's theoretical framing.
Recruit participants, and co-lead and help coordinate storytelling workshops with c.8 Greater Manchester community groups.
Co-develop a creative toolkit.
Co-develop and run focus groups exploring circular fashion policy.
Manage research data securely, including transcription and anonymisation, in line with data protection and research ethics requirements.
Act as lead or co-author on peer-reviewed journal articles.
Contribute to public storytelling events, community dissemination workshops and an industry-facing forum.
Set up and run the project's social media presence. 

Key Skills & Experiences

We are looking for someone with a good understanding of, and genuine interest in, emotion, narrative and clothing consumption behaviour, ideally with an interest in circular fashion and sustainability.

Essential

A doctoral qualification (held or nearing completion) in a relevant social science or humanities discipline (e.g. Sociology, Fashion/Cultural Studies, Human Geography or Marketing/Consumer Research).
Qualitative research skills, including interviewing, workshop or focus-group facilitation, and narrative or thematic analysis.
Experience of, or willingness to be trained in, narrative inquiry methods.
Ability to build trust and work sensitively with a wide range of community groups, including vulnerable participants, and to maintain respectful relationships with group leads and members.
Strong organisational skills, with the ability to coordinate concurrent workstreams (workshops, focus groups, transcription and toolkit production) to deadline.
Confidence handling sensitive personal data securely and in line with data protection and research ethics requirements.
Strong academic writing skills, with the ability to co-author peer-reviewed journal articles.
Confidence engaging with stakeholders across academia, community organisations, local government and the fashion industry, and communicating with academic and non-academic audiences.
Comfortable setting up and maintaining a project website and Instagram presence.
A self-starter, able to work independently and across two institutions.
Willingness to undertake safeguarding training and to take part in academic meetings and networks that extend the reach of the research.

Desirable

Experience of community-based or participatory research with diverse or underrepresented groups.
Experience of public engagement outputs, such as podcasts, blogs, live storytelling events or exhibitions.
Experience of working with local government, combined authorities or policy stakeholders.
Familiarity with institutional research data management systems and FAIR data principles. 

To learn more about this exciting opportunity and benefits we offer, please read the JD provided below. 

Application & Assessment

To apply, submit your CV and supporting statement outlining how best you met the criteria, via our online portal. Please note applications received without a supporting statement will not be considered.
Assessment will include a competency-based interview round. The interview date is Friday 27 November 2026. As part of the interview, candidates will be presented with a research scenario and asked to develop a brief qualitative research plan to assess their creative and practical research design skills.
For informal enquiries about this vacancy, please contact Dr Benjamin Wild on b.wild@mmu.ac.uk 

If you would like to join our people and share our ambition, we would love to hear from you!

 

Further Information

Manchester Metropolitan University fosters an inclusive culture of belonging that promotes equity and celebrates diversity. We value a diverse workforce for the innovation and diversity of thought it brings and welcome applications from local and international communities, including those from Black, Asian, and Minority Ethnic backgrounds, disabled people, and LGBTQ+ individuals.

We support a range of flexible working arrangements, including hybrid and tailored schedules, which can be discussed with your line manager. If you require reasonable adjustments during the recruitment process or in your role, please let us know so we can provide appropriate support.

Postdoctoral Research Associate
Edinburgh, Midlothian, United Kingdom

Role: 
Postdoctoral Research Associate

Grade and Salary:
 Grade 7 (£38,448 - £46,970) per annum

FTE and working pattern:
 1 FTE (full time - 35 hours per week) fixed term until 2030

Holiday Entitlement:
 

33 days annual leave plus 9 buildings-closed days (and Christmas Eve when it falls on a weekday). Use our total rewards calculator:  

https://www.hw.ac.uk/about/work/total-rewards-calculator.htm

 to see the value of benefits provided by Heriot-Watt University.

 

Purpose of Role

Applications are invited for a Postdoctoral Research Assistant (PDRA) position, funded through the Leverhulme Trust research grant “Tackling questions and conjectures around Gromov-hyperbolicity,” led by Dr. Alessandro Sisto. The post will be held at the Department of Mathematics of Heriot Watt University and at the Maxwell Institute, Edinburgh, and will be for a fixed term of up to 36 months (3 years). The successful applicant is expected to start on July 1st, 2027. 

Geometric group theory is a field that studies groups by realizing them as symmetries of spaces with a rich geometry, and finds itself at the interface between algebra, geometry, topology, and combinatorics.

The overall objective of the project is to tackle the main open questions in geometric group theory that relates to hyperbolicity, and in the process to further our understanding of groups with hyperbolic features. Specifically, the projects focus on hierarchically hyperbolic structures, quasi-isometry invariant random processes on groups, and Dehn fillings and related constructions.

The project leader is happy to be contacted for informal discussions about the position – email at 

a.sisto@hw.ac.uk

 

Key Duties & Responsibilities

You will conduct and disseminate research in geometric group theory and related fields (write and submit academic articles, give talks at seminars and conferences). You will work on questions related to the proposed project together with the project leader and his collaborators (more detail on the project below) and develop your own research directions. 

You will actively engage with the thriving research community in geometric group theory of Heriot Watt University and the Maxwell Institute by attending seminars, organizing research events, as appropriate. 

You will be offered the opportunity to further your professional and personal development skills, and the project leader will support the successful applicant in their academic, scientific, and professional growth. 

This position has no teaching load but comes with the possibility of taking on some light teaching duties, should the candidate wish to gain teaching experience.

Essential & Desirable Criteria

Essential

Applicants should hold (or be about to obtain) a PhD in mathematics.

Evidence of excellent work in geometric group theory. 

Excellent oral and written communication skills.

Ability to work both independently and as part of a group.

Desirable

Evidence of work on hyperbolic features of groups. 

Evidence of research on topics that complement the existing expertise of the Heriot Watt geometric group theory team.

How to Apply

Applications can be submitted up to 11:55pm (UK time) on Sunday 29th November

Please submit your CV & covering letter via the Heriot-Watt on-line recruitment. Applications must contain: 

A CV (max. 5 pages) containing a list of publications. The applicant may add to their CV the contact details (name, institution, email address) of up to two people who may be contacted for recommendation letters.

A research statement (max. 5 pages) containing a description of past results as well as future research directions.

We may close this vacancy early if we receive a high volume of applications. We therefore encourage you to submit your application promptly.

The interviews are anticipated to be conducted mid-January 2027.

We recognise that many candidates use AI tools during the application process and are comfortable with AI being used as a supporting aid. However, we want to hear from you, not AI.

Your application should be an authentic representation of your skills, experience and achievements. Applications that appear to have been fully generated by AI may not accurately reflect your suitability for the role and are therefore discouraged.

At interview, candidates will be expected to discuss and provide evidence of the experience, skills and examples included in their application.

We welcome and will consider flexible working patterns e.g., part-time working and job share options.

Heriot-Watt University is committed to securing equality of opportunity in employment and to the creation of an environment in which individuals are selected, trained, promoted, appraised, and otherwise treated on the sole basis of their relevant merits and abilities.  Equality and diversity are all about maximising potential and creating a culture of inclusion for all.

Heriot-Watt University values diversity across our university community and welcomes applications from all sectors of society, particularly from underrepresented groups. For more information, please see our website 

https://www.hw.ac.uk/uk/services/equality-diversity.htm

 and also our award-winning work in Disability Inclusive Science Careers 

https://disc.hw.ac.uk/

 .

Use our total rewards calculator: 

https://www.hw.ac.uk/about/work/total-rewards-calculator.htm

 to see the value of benefits provided by Heriot-Watt University.

About the Team

The PDRA will work closely with the project leader and his network of collaborators. The Geometric Group Theory team at Heriot Watt University consists of five permanent faculty (Laura Ciobanu, Matthew Cordes, Francesco Fournier-Facio, Alexandre Martin, Alessandro Sisto), as well as several PhD students. The team is also a member of the North British Geometric Group Theory research network, which organises regular events bringing together mathematicians from several institutions: Aberdeen, Glasgow, St Andrews, Durham, etc. 

The department of mathematics at Heriot Watt is part of the Maxwell Institute for Mathematical Sciences, an institute bringing together the mathematical activities of Heriot Watt University and the University of Edinburgh. The Maxwell Institute coordinates a wide spectrum of activities, including a large graduate school, numerous seminar series, Knowledge Exchange and outreach events, and distinguished lecture series. 

Heriot Watt has also a central role in the running of the International Centre for Mathematical Sciences (ICMS), a world-renowned conference centre. The ICMS further enriches the research environment of the Maxwell Institute by attracting a constant flow of national and international research visitors. 

About Heriot-Watt University

At Heriot-Watt we are passionate about our values and look to them to connect our people globally and to help us collaborate and celebrate our success through working together. Our research programmes can deliver real world impact which is achieved through the diversity of our international community and the recognition of creative talent that connects our global team.

Our flourishing community will give you the freedom to challenge and to bring your enterprising mind and to help our partners with solutions that can be applied now and in the future. Join us and Heriot Watt will provide you with a platform to thrive and work in a way that also helps you live your life in balance with well-being and inclusiveness at the heart of our global community.

Would you like to work on the fundamental mechanisms of triboelectrification at the atomic and molecular scales using Density Functional Theory to elucidate the underlying triboelectric charge transfer mechanisms? Do you have experience in ab-initio electronic structure modelling using Density Functional Theory to understand and predict materials properties? Are you interested in working in a multidisciplinary team proactively tackling technical tasks in parallel?

Electrostatic charge accumulation in powders and grains, due to collisional and sliding contacts of surfaces of solids, commonly known as triboelectrification, is a nuisance and source of hazards, and at the same time, it has great potential for exploitation, as in the fast-growing technology of Tribo-Electric Nano-Generators (TENG). The former adversely affects manufacturability, due to issues such as downtime, valuable product loss and negative environmental impact, whilst for the latter, the identification of durable and efficient functional materials is highly desirable. The capability to predict triboelectrification tendency of materials provides a great competitive edge in advanced manufacturing across a wide range of industries from food and pharmaceuticals to additive manufacturing, polymers and TENG.

 About the role 

 Reporting to Professor Simon Newstead (Principal Investigator) and Dr Jo Parker (Senior Research Scientist), the post holder will be a member of the Newstead group in the Department of Biochemistry and Kavli Institute for Nanoscience, which studies the structure, mechanism and cellular biology of solute carrier (SLC) transporters. The post holder will lead the group's native mass spectrometry research, a discrete area within a larger programme on how SLC transporters are folded, modified, trafficked and regulated in mammalian cells.

 This full-time fixed-term post is funded by the Wellcome Trust for up to 12 months in the first instance.

 The actual starting salary offered will be based on qualifications and relevant skills acquired and will also be determined by the funding available. 

 About you 

 You will hold, or be near completion of, a PhD/DPhil in biophysical chemistry, analytical chemistry, structural biology or a related discipline, with substantial experience in native top-down mass spectrometry using high-resolution hybrid Orbitrap instrumentation, including Thermo Fisher Orbitrap UHMR and Ascend platforms. You will demonstrate expertise in native mass spectrometry sample preparation, advanced fragmentation techniques, quantitative analysis of protein modifications and lipid interactions, alongside experience in proteomics, lipidomics and membrane protein expression and purification. You will also possess strong computational and data-analysis skills, including scientific software development, ideally using Python. Experience in SLC transporter research, glycoproteomics and open-source software development, together with a strong publication record, would be advantageous.

 The Research Officer will provide high-quality administration and coordination for a range of research activities across the Faculty of Humanities and Social Sciences. Working closely with academic and professional services colleagues, the post holder will support research activity throughout the research life cycle.

 Key responsibilities include supporting research grant applications and administration, advising on pre- and post-award procedures, coordinating research committees and peer review processes, supporting Research Excellence Framework (REF) activities, and maintaining accurate records of research activity and funding applications. The role will also contribute to research events, communications and other activities that support the Faculty's research strategy.

 You will be educated to degree level or possess equivalent professional experience, together with substantial administrative experience in a research support or comparable environment.  The successful candidate will have experience of working with a range of stakeholders, a collaborative approach to working, and a commitment to providing excellent support to researchers and colleagues.

 The Faculty of Humanities and Social Sciences combines research excellence with a strong commitment to growth, innovation and diversity in its educational activities. Public engagement, partnerships, cross-disciplinary collaboration and the generation of research with broad public benefit are central to the Faculty's success.

 At Queen Mary University of London, we believe that a diversity of ideas helps us achieve the previously unthinkable.

 We continue to embrace diversity of thought and opinion in everything we do, in the belief that when views collide, disciplines interact, and perspectives intersect, truly original thought takes form.

 We are looking to appoint an independent Research Fellow with excellent interpersonal skills to join our vibrant research team and drive impactful research into sudden and unexpected deaths in infancy and childhood. 

 This project, which is funded by the National Institute for Health Research, is the first of its kind, has national reach and importance, and represents the collaboration of multiple stakeholders across the academic, clinical, charitable and policy sectors. 

 After the sudden death of their child, families often do not have ready access to support and care, and professionals supporting families can be at risk for mental distress and lack support. This is the first study focusing on really understanding experiences, needs and outcomes for families; and will develop recommendations for robust bereavement support and care. The role will mainly involve qualitative and quantitative data analysis and writing for publication, and report writing for the funder. Location: COVENTRY, GB, CV4 7AL

Company: University of Warwick

Job Title: Research Fellow (USA)

Reference:  338             

Department: Sociology

Contract Type: Fixed-term contract

Fixed Term End Date: 31 December 2028

Hours: Full-time (1.0 FTE)

Closing Date: Thursday 5 November 2026                        

Full time Salary Range: £35,608.00 - £46,049.00 per annum

About the Role

We are seeking to appoint a Research Fellow to work on the ERC-funded project RAIDS: Religious Authority in Extractive Industry Struggles, led by Professor Claire Blencowe in the Department of Sociology, University of Warwick.

 

RAIDS will explore the role of religion as a ‘weapon’ of both powerful corporations and marginalised communities involved in social and ecological struggles over mines or mining infrastructure. The project advances understanding of the range of authority and soft-power mechanisms at play in the contemporary extractivism. It investigates whether and how extractive industries and religious nationalisms support each other today. Working in partnership with communities engaged in existing struggles the project will amplify the knowledge and experience of marginalised front-line communities. This includes taking seriously forms of religious or spiritual activism that have too often been dismissed by modern social science, as well as supporting knowledge exchange and solidarity between communities engaged in disparate struggles.

 

The research fellow will be employed for two years to conduct research on religion in extractive industry struggles in the USA. We are looking for engaged activist-scholars who are able to work closely and respectfully with mine-affected communities, participating with and supporting the community's existing activism.

 

You are invited to propose your own case studies as part of your application, drawing upon your existing connections or affinities with mine-affected communities. Once appointed, we will work together as a team to finalise the case study design and carry out the research encompassing: critical cultural/authority studies investigation of the 'soft' power backing contemporary mining corporations; participatory research with mine affected communities exploring the ways that they can and do engage religious or spiritual practice, organisation or wisdom in their struggles; and co-producing analysis and outputs with the mine-affected communities.

During a six-month preparatory period the fellow will conduct a literature review, ethics clearance, and training in participatory research methods. A year of empirical research will follow, including: participatory observation with each case-study community; co-hosting participatory theory workshops; interviews; and online critical/investigative analysis. A final six-month period focuses on completion of outputs including at least one lead-authored journal article, data packages for each case study, news stories, and content for the project website and co-authored book, as well as future planning.

 

The post is full-time, fixed-term appointments for 24 months commencing January 2027.

 

For further information or informal enquiries, please contact Professor Claire Blencowe (C.Blencowe@warwick.ac.uk).

 

For details on the experience and skills required, please refer to the job description (link here).

 

About You

 

PhD Status

 

If you are near submission of your PhD, or have not yet had it conferred, any offers of employment will be made at Research Assistant level, at the highest spinal point of pay grade 5 (£34,610 per annum).

 

Upon receipt of evidence confirming the successful award of your PhD, you will be promoted to Research Fellow, at the lowest spinal point of grade 6 (£35,608 per annum).

 

You will be a rigorous, reflective and collaborative researcher in a relevant field. You will have experience of qualitative research methods such as interviews, ethnography, participant observation, documentary or archival research, participatory methods, digital methods or community-based research.  You will also be able to work sensitively and ethically with communities affected by environmental harm, displacement, marginalisation or political conflict.

 

For the USA post, expertise in the USA, extractive industries, religion, Indigenous sovereignty, settler colonialism, environmental justice, racial capitalism, Christian nationalism, petro-cultures or pipeline politics is desirable.

 

We are looking for candidates who can work independently and collaboratively, communicate clearly with academic and non-academic audiences and contribute to high-quality research outputs, public engagement and the wider aims of the RAIDS project.

About the Project

The global rush for minerals often overlooks the role of religious authority as a hidden force shaping local resistance, corporate power and extractive industry struggles. The ERC-funded RAIDS project (Religious Authority in Extractive Industry Struggles) will explore how religion serves as a potent ‘weapon’ for both marginalised communities and powerful extractive interests.

 

The project will analyse eight diverse mining disputes across Brazil, India, Indonesia, and the USA. Using a decolonial-feminist approach, it will centre the voices of those on the front lines of mineral extraction and examine how spiritual narratives influence struggles over land, labour and justice. In the context of climate catastrophe and the post-carbon transition, RAIDS will offer new insights into the systematic inequalities connected to mineral extraction today.

 

RAIDS will be carried out over five years, commencing in September 2026 and will be led by Professor Claire Blencowe. The project team will include a project administrator, a project producer and four postdoctoral research fellows, who will work alongside Professor Blencowe to finalise the case study design and carry out the research.

 

The research will encompass critical culture and authority studies investigating the ‘soft’ power behind contemporary mining corporations, participatory research with mine-affected communities exploring how religious or spiritual practice, organisations and wisdom are used in their struggles, and the co-production of analysis and outputs with mine-affected communities.

 

To find out more, please visit our website at: https://warwick.ac.uk/fac/soc/sociology/staff/blencowe/raids/

About the Department

The Department of Sociology at the University of Warwick is one of the UK's leading Sociology departments, recognised nationally and internationally for the quality of its teaching and research. We are ranked 8th in the UK for Sociology in The Times and Sunday Times Good University Guide 2026 and among the top 100 Sociology departments globally in the QS World University Rankings by Subject 2026. In REF2021, 100% of our research environment was judged to be conducive to producing research of world-leading or internationally excellent quality.

 

Our research and teaching engage with some of the most pressing challenges facing contemporary societies, including inequality, migration, race and ethnicity, gender, health, sustainability, technology and social justice. The Department hosts a wide programme of research activity and seminars throughout the year, delivered through our research clusters and centres. We are also expanding our teaching portfolio, with two new undergraduate programmes due to launch in the next academic year (2026-27).

 

Sociology has a strong culture of community and engagement that extends beyond teaching and research. Our Care Collective provides an informal space for collegial support, and our Green Team is responsible for identifying and implementing departmental actions that contribute to environmental sustainability.

We are proud to hold an Athena Swan Silver Award, recognising our commitment to advancing gender equality and creating an inclusive working and learning environment. As part of our ongoing commitment to equality, diversity and inclusion, we are currently working towards Athena Swan Gold accreditation.

 

We strive to create a culture in which everyone is treated with dignity and respect, differences are valued, and all members of our community are supported to thrive. We warmly welcome applications from candidates of all backgrounds.

 

To find out more about the Department of Sociology, please visit our website: https://warwick.ac.uk/fac/soc/sociology/.

How to Apply

To apply please complete your essential personal details and attach a CV and cover letter by the closing date stated. Please ensure your CV includes your most recent employment experience along with any additional relevant experience and education history.   

We will review applications throughout the advertising period and may contact shortlisted candidates before the closing date. We therefore encourage interested applicants to submit their application as early as possible. We reserve the right to close this vacancy early should we receive a sufficient number of suitable applications. 

 

Applicants are asked to propose two extractive industry struggles that you could successfully research as case studies, drawing upon your existing connections, or affinities, with mine-affected communities. Please read further information on the research project so that you understand where these case studies sit in the project. In your application you do not need to propose a methodology for researching your case studies, you simply need to:

Briefly describe each extractive industry struggle 
Tell us why it might be promising as a site to research religious authority in extractive industry struggles
Tell us why you personally would be a good fit to work with that community

We will provide you with a great range of benefits, which include an attractive pension scheme, a generous holiday allowance plus Christmas closure, excellent learning and development opportunities, and savings on a wide range of products and services. We offer a generous maternity/paternity/adoption/parental leave policy, and onsite childcare facilities.

 

We recognise the importance of a healthy work/life balance and offer you access to flexible working, for more information click here.

 

We are proud to say that we are a Living Wage employer.

 

If you are considering relocating to the UK, read our Relocation Guide to find out more about what Warwick has to offer and what might be involved in the process.

 

Warwick is committed to building an organisation of mutual respect and dignity, promoting a welcoming, diverse, and inclusive working and learning environment.  We recognise that everyone is different in a variety of visible and non-visible ways, and that those differences are to be recognised, respected, and valued.  Where possible, we go beyond legislation to provide a place where everyone can thrive, supporting all staff to achieve their full potential. We aspire to remove economic, social, and cultural barriers that may otherwise prevent people from succeeding.

 

We therefore welcome and encourage applications from all communities regardless of culture, background, age, disability, sex/gender, gender identity or expression, ethnicity, religion/belief, or sexual or romantic orientation. To find out more about our social inclusion work at Warwick visit our webpages here.

 

The University currently holds a Race Equality Charter Bronze Award, Athena Swan Sliver Award and a Disability Smart Bronze Award. Further information on all of the University's Awards and Accreditations can be found here. The University of Warwick is also one of the six founder institutions of the EUTOPIA European University Alliance.
